text:
maya: Heads up, EU warm pools are failing warmup since the IAM shared-role change at ~08:20. Nodes can't decrypt bootstrap secrets, hitting KMS denies and audit spike. Anyone seeing this?
cheng: Seen it. Multiple node join errors in eu-west-1. Autoscaler is spinning other regions up to keep capacity.
alex: Oof — that’ll blow up cross-region egress costs. :grimacing:
oncall-sre: Confirmed. Warmup fail logs: 
```
2026-03-21T08:22:11Z node-init ERROR decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: Caller is not authorized to use kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:...
2026-03-21T08:22:12Z kubelet WARN failed to register: bootstrap token missing
```
ops-bot: Policy-rollout bot: "iam-policy/shared-node-provisioning:deploy" finished (08:19) by security.
security: That rollout tightened AssumeRole conditions to require vpc:sourceIp and tag:env for the shared role. We thought it was safe — why are nodes missing tags at join time?
maya: The node bootstrap path runs before we tag instances (taint/label logic runs later). The assume role condition now blocks the instance profile used by the provisioning job.
irene: This exact ordering dependency was noted in the PR but we scoped it as low risk. Clearly not.
cheng: Quick mitigation idea: relax the AssumeRole vpc:sourceIp condition for the shared role for 2 hours, or use an explicit temporary role for bootstrap.
alex: Relaxing will open a narrow window; security, can we get an exception? We’re at ~150 warm failures and autoscaler already launched 12 nodes in us-west-2. Cost estimate ~= +$6k/day if this continues.
security: We can do a scoped exception limited to the EU warmpool agent principal + only eu-west-1 CIDR. Need a JIRA and an audit annotation.
oncall-sre: Meanwhile, can we fallback to cached prefixes? Some services have prefix cache but node bootstrap doesn't.
maya: Another angle — KMS key policy denies decrypts from instance role because role arn changed slightly after the policy refactor earlier this week. That explains the AccessDenied too. Two simultaneous breakages.
cheng: Great. So: (1) temporary IAM assume role relaxation for bootstrapping, (2) add old role ARN to KMS key policy for decrypt, (3) backfill instance tagging order in bootstrap flow.
alex: Can someone do (1) now? I opened https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1842 for the exception.
security: I can create the exception but need an owner and TTL. Who owns warm-pool bootstrap? maya?
maya: I'll own TTL and rollback. Propose 2 hours and then automatic revocation.
ops-bot: Change request created: CR-2026-342 (assume-role exception until 2026-03-21T10:30Z). Requires approval from @security and @oncall-sre.
security: Approving now. Please annotate the change with reason and link to INFRA-1842.
irene: I'll push the temporary KMS key policy add to include the legacy role ARN (only decrypt). Patch: 
```
kms:PutKeyPolicy -> add Principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/legacy-node-provisioner with Action kms:Decrypt
```
cheng: After that we should see nodes decrypting and joining. Any plan to prevent recurrence?
maya: Follow-ups: (A) fix bootstrap ordering to tag instances earlier (B) add a canary job that simulates bootstrap under tightened AssumeRole conditions before policies roll out (C) update runbook with service-dependency matrix so policy PRs check bootstrap paths.
alex: Also reduce audit log retention for bootstrap KMS denies (they're noisy) but keep sampled hits for security. Cost side: set a temporary budget alert to avoid surprise billing for cross-region autoscaling.
security: Agree on the runbook items. We'll require canary green before any further AssumeRole deployments. Also adding explicit owner checks in PR templates.
oncall-sre: FYI: I applied the temp exception at 08:30 and the KMS patch at 08:36. Warm pool started recovering at 08:42. Current recovery metrics: 70% of previously failing nodes are healthy, autoscaler is stopped from further cross-region adds.
maya: Monitoring: 
- warmpool_join_failures: 18 -> 5 in last 10m
- cross_region_instances_started: 12 -> 12 (stopped)
- projected daily egress cost delta: +$1.1k remaining (already incurred)
alex: Nice work. Postmortem notes: include cost number, timeline, and the PR that tightened AssumeRole. Tag product/infra-costs for chargeback.
security: We'll run a constrained stress canary in staging with the new conditions tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Please add test vectors to the canary job that emulate late tags and older role ARNs.
irene: Opening follow-up tickets: INFRA-1843 (bootstrap tag ordering), INFRA-1844 (canary before assume-role rollout), INFRA-1845 (kms key policy hygiene).
maya: Closing loop: thanks for quick approvals. I'll handle rollback TTL and file the incident blameless postmortem. :thumbsup:
alex: And reminder — let's avoid policy refactors without a bootstrap dependency checklist. Learned the hard way. :facepalm:
ops-bot: Incident tracker updated: INC-2026-589, severity: P2, owner: maya.
security: Adding a short query to audit logs to find any other keys/policies with assume role conditions that might break bootstrap flows. Will report back in #eng-security. :mag:
